To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GHRH receptor (GHRH-R) gene does not contain mutations in human GH‐secereting pituitary adenoma.
somatic mutations of GHRH‐r are not involved in the development of GH‐secre ting pituitary tumours.
we did not identify somatic mutations in the GHRH receptor gene in a cohort of GH‐secre ting pituitary adenoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of GPCRs in the development of pituitary tumours.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate somatotroph proliferation in normal physiology and pathophysiology.
the molecular basis of somatotropinomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no activating somatic mutations of GHRH‐receptors in human GH‐secereting pituitary adenoma.
the GHRH receptor is a normal gene in GH‐producing pituitary adenoma and no mutations were detected in the GHRH gene.
GHRH‐receptors are not involved in the development of human GH‐producing pituitary adenoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
no activating mutations in the GHRH receptor gene have been found in GH‐secreteing pituitary adenoma.
we have not found mutations in GHRH‐r in GH‐secereting adenomas.
we were unable to find any somatic mutations in the GHRH receptor gene in GH secreting pituitary tumours.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GHRH‐receptor gene mutations are not a frequent event in human GH‐secreteing adenomas.
GHRH‐receptor mutations do not appear to be involved in the pathogenesis of somatotropinomas.
the GHRH receptor does not appear to play a role in the development of human somatotroph adenomas, at least not in a manner similar to that of the GHRHR in mice.
